title: NGC 6188 glows crimson
caption: Emission nebula NGC 6188, imaged by the ESO 3.6-meter telescope

recognition.text: Published in the ESO image archive. No published rating.

story: This image shows the emission nebula NGC 6188, photographed long ago with ESO's 3.6-meter telescope at the La Silla observatory in Chile. The nebula lies about 4,000 light-years away in the southern constellation of Ara.

An emission nebula is a cloud of gas that gives off its own light rather than simply reflecting the light of nearby stars. In NGC 6188, the light comes from within. Stars embedded in the nebula emit radiation that heats the gases around them, and the energized gas glows in response. Without those stars, the cloud would stay dark.
Because the picture is an old one, it is also a piece of ESO's own history, taken with one of the telescopes at La Silla long before many of the images in this collection.
scale: The source lists a distance of 4000 light years, so the light in this picture set out roughly 4,000 years ago.

understand.summary: This image was taken with the ESO 3.6-meter telescope at La Silla. The filters and color mapping are not published.
understand.eye: A long telescope exposure gathers far more light than the eye, so the nebula's faint glow appears far brighter than it would to an observer.
